# Dynamic Programming or DP
Last Updated :  25 Jul, 2025
Comments
Improve

Report
Dynamic Programming is an algorithmic technique with the following properties.
  * It is mainly an optimization over plain recursion. Wherever we see a recursive solution that has repeated calls for the same inputs, we can optimize it using Dynamic Programming. 
  * The idea is to simply store the results of subproblems so that we do not have to re-compute them when needed later. This simple optimization typically reduces time complexities from exponential to polynomial. 
  * Some popular problems solved using Dynamic Programming are [Fibonacci Numbers,](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/program-for-nth-fibonacci-number/) Diff Utility ([Longest Common Subsequence](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/longest-common-subsequence-dp-4/)), [Bellman–Ford Shortest Path](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/bellman-ford-algorithm-dp-23/), [Floyd Warshall](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/floyd-warshall-algorithm-dp-16/), [Edit Distance](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/edit-distance-dp-5/) and [Matrix Chain Multiplication](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/matrix-chain-multiplication-dp-8/).

# Introduction to Dynamic Programming[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/intro-to-dp.html#introduction-to-dynamic-programming "Permanent link")
The essence of dynamic programming is to avoid repeated calculation. Often, dynamic programming problems are naturally solvable by recursion. In such cases, it's easiest to write the recursive solution, then save repeated states in a lookup table. This process is known as top-down dynamic programming with memoization. That's read "memoization" (like we are writing in a memo pad) not memorization.
One of the most basic, classic examples of this process is the fibonacci sequence. Its recursive formulation is  f(n)=f(n−1)+f(n−2)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2)$ where  n≥2<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math>$n \ge 2$ and  f(0)=0<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>$f(0)=0$ and  f(1)=1<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>$f(1)=1$ . In C++, this would be expressed as:
```
int f(int n) {
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    if (n == 1) return 1;
    return f(n - 1) + f(n - 2);
}

```

The runtime of this recursive function is exponential - approximately  O(2n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(2^n)$ since one function call (  f(n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(n)$ ) results in 2 similarly sized function calls ( f(n−1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(n-1)$ and  f(n−2)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(n-2)$ ).
## Speeding up Fibonacci with Dynamic Programming (Memoization)[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/intro-to-dp.html#speeding-up-fibonacci-with-dynamic-programming-memoization "Permanent link")
Our recursive function currently solves fibonacci in exponential time. This means that we can only handle small input values before the problem becomes too difficult. For instance,  f(29)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>29</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(29)$ results in _over 1 million_ function calls!
To increase the speed, we recognize that the number of subproblems is only  O(n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n)$ . That is, in order to calculate  f(n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(n)$ we only need to know  f(n−1),f(n−2),…,f(0)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(n-1),f(n-2), \dots ,f(0)$ . Therefore, instead of recalculating these subproblems, we solve them once and then save the result in a lookup table. Subsequent calls will use this lookup table and immediately return a result, thus eliminating exponential work! 
Each recursive call will check against a lookup table to see if the value has been calculated. This is done in  O(1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(1)$ time. If we have previously calculated it, return the result, otherwise, we calculate the function normally. The overall runtime is  O(n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n)$ . This is an enormous improvement over our previous exponential time algorithm!
```
const int MAXN = 100;
bool found[MAXN];
int memo[MAXN];

int f(int n) {
    if (found[n]) return memo[n];
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    if (n == 1) return 1;

    found[n] = true;
    return memo[n] = f(n - 1) + f(n - 2);
}

```

With our new memoized recursive function,  f(29)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>29</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(29)$ , which used to result in _over 1 million calls_ , now results in _only 57_ calls, nearly _20,000 times_ fewer function calls! Ironically, we are now limited by our data type.  f(46)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>46</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$f(46)$ is the last fibonacci number that can fit into a signed 32-bit integer.
Typically, we try to save states in arrays, if possible, since the lookup time is  O(1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(1)$ with minimal overhead. However, more generically, we can save states any way we like. Other examples include binary search trees (`map` in C++) or hash tables (`unordered_map` in C++).
An example of this might be:
```
unordered_map<int, int> memo;
int f(int n) {
    if (memo.count(n)) return memo[n];
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    if (n == 1) return 1;

    return memo[n] = f(n - 1) + f(n - 2);
}

```

Or analogously:
```
map<int, int> memo;
int f(int n) {
    if (memo.count(n)) return memo[n];
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    if (n == 1) return 1;

    return memo[n] = f(n - 1) + f(n - 2);
}

```

Both of these will almost always be slower than the array-based version for a generic memoized recursive function. These alternative ways of saving state are primarily useful when saving vectors or strings as part of the state space.
The layman's way of analyzing the runtime of a memoized recursive function is:
work per subproblem∗number of subproblems<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><mtext>work per subproblem</mtext><mo>∗</mo><mtext>number of subproblems</mtext></math>$$\text{work per subproblem} * \text{number of subproblems}$$
Using a binary search tree (map in C++) to save states will technically result in  O(nlog⁡n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>log</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n \log n)$ as each lookup and insertion will take  O(log⁡n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>log</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(\log n)$ work and with  O(n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n)$ unique subproblems we have  O(nlog⁡n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>log</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n \log n)$ time.
This approach is called top-down, as we can call the function with a query value and the calculation starts going from the top (queried value) down to the bottom (base cases of the recursion), and makes shortcuts via memoization on the way.
## Bottom-up Dynamic Programming[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/intro-to-dp.html#bottom-up-dynamic-programming "Permanent link")
Until now you've only seen top-down dynamic programming with memoization. However, we can also solve problems with bottom-up dynamic programming. Bottom-up is exactly the opposite of top-down, you start at the bottom (base cases of the recursion), and extend it to more and more values.
To create a bottom-up approach for fibonacci numbers, we initialize the base cases in an array. Then, we simply use the recursive definition on array:
```
const int MAXN = 100;
int fib[MAXN];

int f(int n) {
    fib[0] = 0;
    fib[1] = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) fib[i] = fib[i - 1] + fib[i - 2];

    return fib[n];
}

```

Of course, as written, this is a bit silly for two reasons: Firstly, we do repeated work if we call the function more than once. Secondly, we only need to use the two previous values to calculate the current element. Therefore, we can reduce our memory from  O(n)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n)$ to  O(1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(1)$ . 
An example of a bottom-up dynamic programming solution for fibonacci which uses  O(1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(1)$ memory might be:
```
const int MAX_SAVE = 3;
int fib[MAX_SAVE];

int f(int n) {
    fib[0] = 0;
    fib[1] = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++)
        fib[i % MAX_SAVE] = fib[(i - 1) % MAX_SAVE] + fib[(i - 2) % MAX_SAVE];

    return fib[n % MAX_SAVE];
}

```

Note that we've changed the constant from `MAXN` TO `MAX_SAVE`. This is because the total number of elements we need to access is only 3. It no longer scales with the size of input and is, by definition,  O(1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(1)$ memory. Additionally, we use a common trick (using the modulo operator) only maintaining the values we need.
That's it. That's the basics of dynamic programming: Don't repeat the work you've done before.
One of the tricks to getting better at dynamic programming is to study some of the classic examples.

# 动态规划部分简介
本章将介绍介绍动态规划（Dynamic Programming, DP）及其解决的问题、根据其设计的算法及优化。
动态规划是一种通过把原问题分解为相对简单的子问题的方式求解复杂问题的方法。
由于动态规划并不是某种具体的算法，而是一种解决特定问题的方法，因此它会出现在各式各样的数据结构中，与之相关的题目种类也更为繁杂。
在 OI 中，计数等非最优化问题的递推解法也常被不规范地称作 DP，因此本章将它们一并列出。事实上，动态规划与其它类型的递推的确有很多相似之处，学习时可以注意它们之间的异同。

# Knapsack Problem[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#knapsack-problem "Permanent link")
Prerequisite knowledge: [Introduction to Dynamic Programming](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/intro-to-dp.html)
## Introduction[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#introduction "Permanent link")
Consider the following example:
###  [[USACO07 Dec] Charm Bracelet](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/6144)[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#usaco07-dec-charm-bracelet "Permanent link")
There are  n<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>$n$ distinct items and a knapsack of capacity  W<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math>$W$ . Each item has 2 attributes, weight ( wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$w_{i}$ ) and value ( vi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$v_{i}$ ). You have to select a subset of items to put into the knapsack such that the total weight does not exceed the capacity  W<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math>$W$ and the total value is maximized.
In the example above, each object has only two possible states (taken or not taken), corresponding to binary 0 and 1. Thus, this type of problem is called "0-1 knapsack problem".
## 0-1 Knapsack[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#0-1-knapsack "Permanent link")
### Explanation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#explanation "Permanent link")
In the example above, the input to the problem is the following: the weight of  ith<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>i</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></math>$i^{th}$ item  wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$w_{i}$ , the value of  ith<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>i</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></math>$i^{th}$ item  vi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$v_{i}$ , and the total capacity of the knapsack  W<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math>$W$ .
Let  fi,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i, j}$ be the dynamic programming state holding the maximum total value the knapsack can carry with capacity  j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>j</mi></math>$j$ , when only the first  i<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math>$i$ items are considered.
Assuming that all states of the first  i−1<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>$i-1$ items have been processed, what are the options for the  ith<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>i</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></math>$i^{th}$ item?
  * When it is not put into the knapsack, the remaining capacity remains unchanged and total value does not change. Therefore, the maximum value in this case is  fi−1,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i-1, j}$
  * When it is put into the knapsack, the remaining capacity decreases by  wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$w_{i}$ and the total value increases by  vi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$v_{i}$ , so the maximum value in this case is  fi−1,j−wi+vi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>$f_{i-1, j-w_i} + v_i$


From this we can derive the dp transition equation:
fi,j=max(fi−1,j,fi−1,j−wi+vi)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$f_{i, j} = \max(f_{i-1, j}, f_{i-1, j-w_i} + v_i)$$
Further, as  fi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i}$ is only dependent on  fi−1<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i-1}$ , we can remove the first dimension. We obtain the transition rule
fj←max(fj,fj−wi+vi)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$f_j \gets \max(f_j, f_{j-w_i}+v_i)$$
that should be executed in the **decreasing** order of  j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>j</mi></math>$j$ (so that  fj−wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{j-w_i}$ implicitly corresponds to  fi−1,j−wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i-1,j-w_i}$ and not  fi,j−wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i,j-w_i}$ ).
**It is important to understand this transition rule, because most of the transitions for knapsack problems are derived in a similar way.**
### Implementation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#implementation "Permanent link")
The algorithm described can be implemented in  O(nW)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(nW)$ as:
```
for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)
  for (int j = W; j >= w[i]; j--)
    f[j] = max(f[j], f[j - w[i]] + v[i]);

```

Again, note the order of execution. It should be strictly followed to ensure the following invariant: Right before the pair  (i,j)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$(i, j)$ is processed,  fk<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></math>$f_k$ corresponds to  fi,k<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i,k}$ for  k>j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mo>></mo><mi>j</mi></math>$k > j$ , but to  fi−1,k<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i-1,k}$ for  k<j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mo><</mo><mi>j</mi></math>$k < j$ . This ensures that  fj−wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{j-w_i}$ is taken from the  (i−1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$(i-1)$ -th step, rather than from the  i<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math>$i$ -th one.
## Complete Knapsack[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#complete-knapsack "Permanent link")
The complete knapsack model is similar to the 0-1 knapsack, the only difference from the 0-1 knapsack is that an item can be selected an unlimited number of times instead of only once.
We can refer to the idea of 0-1 knapsack to define the state:  fi,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i, j}$ , the maximum value the knapsack can obtain using the first  i<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math>$i$ items with maximum capacity  j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>j</mi></math>$j$ .
It should be noted that although the state definition is similar to that of a 0-1 knapsack, its transition rule is different from that of a 0-1 knapsack.
### Explanation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#explanation_1 "Permanent link")
The trivial approach is, for the first  i<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math>$i$ items, enumerate how many times each item is to be taken. The time complexity of this is  O(n2W)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(n^2W)$ .
This yields the following transition equation:
fi,j=maxk=0∞(fi−1,j−k⋅wi+k⋅vi)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">max</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munderover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$f_{i, j} = \max\limits_{k=0}^{\infty}(f_{i-1, j-k\cdot w_i} + k\cdot v_i)$$
At the same time, it simplifies into a "flat" equation:
fi,j=max(fi−1,j,fi,j−wi+vi)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$f_{i, j} = \max(f_{i-1, j},f_{i, j-w_i} + v_i)$$
The reason this works is that  fi,j−wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i, j-w_i}$ has already been updated by  fi,j−2⋅wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i, j-2\cdot w_i}$ and so on.
Similar to the 0-1 knapsack, we can remove the first dimension to optimize the space complexity. This gives us the same transition rule as 0-1 knapsack.
fj←max(fj,fj−wi+vi)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$f_j \gets \max(f_j, f_{j-w_i}+v_i)$$
### Implementation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#implementation_1 "Permanent link")
The algorithm described can be implemented in  O(nW)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(nW)$ as:
```
for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)
  for (int j = w[i]; j <= W; j++)
    f[j] = max(f[j], f[j - w[i]] + v[i]);

```

Despite having the same transition rule, the code above is incorrect for 0-1 knapsack.
Observing the code carefully, we see that for the currently processed item  i<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math>$i$ and the current state  fi,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i,j}$ , when  j⩾wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>j</mi><mo>⩾</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math>$j\geqslant w_{i}$ ,  fi,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i,j}$ will be affected by  fi,j−wi<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub></math>$f_{i,j-w_{i}}$ . This is equivalent to being able to put item  i<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math>$i$ into the backpack multiple times, which is consistent with the complete knapsack problem and not the 0-1 knapsack problem.
## Multiple Knapsack[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#multiple-knapsack "Permanent link")
Multiple knapsack is also a variant of 0-1 knapsack. The main difference is that there are  ki<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>$k_i$ of each item instead of just  1<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>$1$ .
### Explanation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#explanation_2 "Permanent link")
A very simple idea is: "choose each item  ki<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>$k_i$ times" is equivalent to " ki<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>$k_i$ of the same item is selected one by one". Thus converting it to a 0-1 knapsack model, which can be described by the transition function:
fi,j=maxk=0ki(fi−1,j−k⋅wi+k⋅vi)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></munderover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$f_{i, j} = \max_{k=0}^{k_i}(f_{i-1,j-k\cdot w_i} + k\cdot v_i)$$
The time complexity of this process is  O(W∑i=1nki)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><munderover><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>n</mi></mrow></munderover><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(W\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}k_i)$
### Binary Grouping Optimization[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#binary-grouping-optimization "Permanent link")
We still consider converting the multiple knapsack model into a 0-1 knapsack model for optimization. The time complexity  O(Wn)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(Wn)$ can not be further optimized with the approach above, so we focus on  O(∑ki)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∑</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(\sum k_i)$ component.
Let  Ai,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$A_{i, j}$ denote the  jth<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>j</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></math>$j^{th}$ item split from the  ith<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>i</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></math>$i^{th}$ item. In the trivial approach discussed above,  Ai,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$A_{i, j}$ represents the same item for all  j≤ki<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>$j \leq k_i$ . The main reason for our low efficiency is that we are doing a lot of repetetive work. For example, consider selecting  {Ai,1,Ai,2}<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">}</mo></math>$\\{A_{i, 1},A_{i, 2}\\}$ , and selecting  {Ai,2,Ai,3}<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">}</mo></math>$\\{A_{i, 2}, A_{i, 3}\\}$ . These two situations are completely equivalent. Thus optimizing the splitting method will greatly reduce the time complexity.
The grouping is made more efficient by using binary grouping.
Specifically,  Ai,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$A_{i, j}$ holds  2j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>j</mi></msup></math>$2^j$ individual items ( j∈[0,⌊log2⁡(ki+1)⌋−1]<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌊</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌋</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></math>$j\in[0,\lfloor \log_2(k_i+1)\rfloor-1]$ ).If  ki+1<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>$k_i + 1$ is not an integer power of  2<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>$2$ , another bundle of size  ki−(2⌊log2⁡(ki+1)⌋−1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌊</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$k_i-(2^{\lfloor \log_2(k_i+1)\rfloor}-1)$ is used to make up for it.
Through the above splitting method, it is possible to obtain any sum of  ≤ki<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>$\leq k_i$ items by selecting a few  Ai,j<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>$A_{i, j}$ 's. After splitting each item in the described way, it is sufficient to use 0-1 knapsack method to solve the new formulation of the problem.
This optimization gives us a time complexity of  O(W∑i=1nlog⁡ki)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><munderover><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>n</mi></mrow></munderover><mi>log</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(W\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}\log k_i)$ .
### Implementation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#implementation_2 "Permanent link")
```
index = 0;
for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
  int c = 1, p, h, k;
  cin >> p >> h >> k;
  while (k > c) {
    k -= c;
    list[++index].w = c * p;
    list[index].v = c * h;
    c *= 2;
  }
  list[++index].w = p * k;
  list[index].v = h * k;
}

```

### Monotone Queue Optimization[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#monotone-queue-optimization "Permanent link")
In this optimization, we aim to convert the knapsack problem into a [maximum queue](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/stack_queue_modification.html) one.
For convenience of description, let  gx,y=fi,x⋅wi+y,gx,y′=fi−1,x⋅wi+y<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math>$g_{x, y} = f_{i, x \cdot w_i + y} ,\space g'_{x, y} = f_{i-1, x \cdot w_i + y}$ . Then the transition rule can be written as:
gx,y=maxk=0ki(gx−k,y′+vi⋅k)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></munderover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⋅</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$$g_{x, y} = \max_{k=0}^{k_i}(g'_{x-k, y} + v_i \cdot k)$$
Further, let  Gx,y=gx,y′−vi⋅x<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></math>$G_{x, y} = g'_{x, y} - v_i \cdot x$ . Then the transition rule can be expressed as:
gx,y←maxk=0ki(Gx−k,y)+vi⋅x<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><munderover><mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></munderover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></math>$$g_{x, y} \gets \max_{k=0}^{k_i}(G_{x-k, y}) + v_i \cdot x$$
This transforms into a classic monotone queue optimization form.  Gx,y<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math>$G_{x, y}$ can be calculated in  O(1)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(1)$ , so for a fixed  y<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>$y$ , we can calculate  gx,y<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math>$g_{x, y}$ in  O(⌊Wwi⌋)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mfrac><mi>W</mi><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌋</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(\lfloor \frac{W}{w_i} \rfloor)$ time. Therefore, the complexity of finding all  gx,y<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math>$g_{x, y}$ is  O(⌊Wwi⌋)×O(wi)=O(W)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mfrac><mi>W</mi><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">⌋</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(\lfloor \frac{W}{w_i} \rfloor) \times O(w_i) = O(W)$ . In this way, the total complexity of the algorithm is reduced to  O(nW)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>$O(nW)$ . 
## Mixed Knapsack[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html#mixed-knapsack "Permanent link")
The mixed knapsack problem involves a combination of the three problems described above. That is, some items can only be taken once, some can be taken infinitely, and some can be taken atmost  k<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math>$k$ times.
The problem may seem daunting, but as long as you understand the core ideas of the previous knapsack problems and combine them together, you can do it. The pseudo code for the solution is as:
```
for (each item) {
  if (0-1 knapsack)
    Apply 0-1 knapsack code;
  else if (complete knapsack)
    Apply complete knapsack code;
  else if (multiple knapsack)
    Apply multiple knapsack code;
}

```

# Longest increasing subsequence[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#longest-increasing-subsequence "Permanent link")
We are given an array with $n$ numbers: $a[0 \dots n-1]$. The task is to find the longest, strictly increasing, subsequence in $a$.
Formally we look for the longest sequence of indices $i_1, \dots i_k$ such that
$$i_1 < i_2 < \dots < i_k,\quad a[i_1] < a[i_2] < \dots < a[i_k]$$
In this article we discuss multiple algorithms for solving this task. Also we will discuss some other problems, that can be reduced to this problem.
## Solution in $O(n^2)$ with dynamic programming[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#solution-in-on2-with-dynamic-programming "Permanent link")
Dynamic programming is a very general technique that allows to solve a huge class of problems. Here we apply the technique for our specific task.
First we will search only for the **length** of the longest increasing subsequence, and only later learn how to restore the subsequence itself.
### Finding the length[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#finding-the-length "Permanent link")
To accomplish this task, we define an array $d[0 \dots n-1]$, where $d[i]$ is the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends in the element at index $i$.
Example
$$\begin{array}{ll} a &= \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0, 7, 9, 1\\} \\\ d &= \\{1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 1, 1, 4, 5, 2\\} \end{array}$$
The longest increasing subsequence that ends at index 4 is $\\{3, 4, 5\\}$ with a length of 3, the longest ending at index 8 is either $\\{3, 4, 5, 7, 9\\}$ or $\\{3, 4, 6, 7, 9\\}$, both having length 5, and the longest ending at index 9 is $\\{0, 1\\}$ having length 2.
We will compute this array gradually: first $d[0]$, then $d[1]$, and so on. After this array is computed, the answer to the problem will be the maximum value in the array $d[]$.
So let the current index be $i$. I.e. we want to compute the value $d[i]$ and all previous values $d[0], \dots, d[i-1]$ are already known. Then there are two options:
  * $d[i] = 1$: the required subsequence consists only of the element $a[i]$.
  * $d[i] > 1$: The subsequence will end at $a[i]$, and right before it will be some number $a[j]$ with $j < i$ and $a[j] < a[i]$.
It's easy to see, that the subsequence ending in $a[j]$ will itself be one of the longest increasing subsequences that ends in $a[j]$. The number $a[i]$ just extends that longest increasing subsequence by one number.
Therefore, we can just iterate over all $j < i$ with $a[j] < a[i]$, and take the longest sequence that we get by appending $a[i]$ to the longest increasing subsequence ending in $a[j]$. The longest increasing subsequence ending in $a[j]$ has length $d[j]$, extending it by one gives the length $d[j] + 1$.
$$d[i] = \max_{\substack{j < i \\\\\\\ a[j] < a[i]}} \left(d[j] + 1\right)$$


If we combine these two cases we get the final answer for $d[i]$:
$$d[i] = \max\left(1, \max_{\substack{j < i \\\\\\\ a[j] < a[i]}} \left(d[j] + 1\right)\right)$$
### Implementation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#implementation "Permanent link")
Here is an implementation of the algorithm described above, which computes the length of the longest increasing subsequence.
```
int lis(vector<int> const& a) {
    int n = a.size();
    vector<int> d(n, 1);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
            if (a[j] < a[i])
                d[i] = max(d[i], d[j] + 1);
        }
    }

    int ans = d[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        ans = max(ans, d[i]);
    }
    return ans;
}

```

### Restoring the subsequence[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#restoring-the-subsequence "Permanent link")
So far we only learned how to find the length of the subsequence, but not how to find the subsequence itself.
To be able to restore the subsequence we generate an additional auxiliary array $p[0 \dots n-1]$ that we will compute alongside the array $d[]$. $p[i]$ will be the index $j$ of the second last element in the longest increasing subsequence ending in $i$. In other words the index $p[i]$ is the same index $j$ at which the highest value $d[i]$ was obtained. This auxiliary array $p[]$ points in some sense to the ancestors.
Then to derive the subsequence, we just start at the index $i$ with the maximal $d[i]$, and follow the ancestors until we deduced the entire subsequence, i.e. until we reach the element with $d[i] = 1$.
### Implementation of restoring[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#implementation-of-restoring "Permanent link")
We will change the code from the previous sections a little bit. We will compute the array $p[]$ alongside $d[]$, and afterwards compute the subsequence.
For convenience we originally assign the ancestors with $p[i] = -1$. For elements with $d[i] = 1$, the ancestors value will remain $-1$, which will be slightly more convenient for restoring the subsequence.
```
vector<int> lis(vector<int> const& a) {
    int n = a.size();
    vector<int> d(n, 1), p(n, -1);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
            if (a[j] < a[i] && d[i] < d[j] + 1) {
                d[i] = d[j] + 1;
                p[i] = j;
            }
        }
    }

    int ans = d[0], pos = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        if (d[i] > ans) {
            ans = d[i];
            pos = i;
        }
    }

    vector<int> subseq;
    while (pos != -1) {
        subseq.push_back(a[pos]);
        pos = p[pos];
    }
    reverse(subseq.begin(), subseq.end());
    return subseq;
}

```

### Alternative way of restoring the subsequence[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#alternative-way-of-restoring-the-subsequence "Permanent link")
It is also possible to restore the subsequence without the auxiliary array $p[]$. We can simply recalculate the current value of $d[i]$ and also see how the maximum was reached.
This method leads to a slightly longer code, but in return we save some memory.
## Solution in $O(n \log n)$ with dynamic programming and binary search[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#solution-in-on-log-n-with-dynamic-programming-and-binary-search "Permanent link")
In order to obtain a faster solution for the problem, we construct a different dynamic programming solution that runs in $O(n^2)$, and then later improve it to $O(n \log n)$.
We will use the dynamic programming array $d[0 \dots n]$. This time $d[l]$ doesn't correspond to the element $a[i]$ or to a prefix of the array. $d[l]$ will be the smallest element at which an increasing subsequence of length $l$ ends.
Initially we assume $d[0] = -\infty$ and for all other lengths $d[l] = \infty$.
We will again gradually process the numbers, first $a[0]$, then $a[1]$, etc, and in each step maintain the array $d[]$ so that it is up to date.
Example
Given the array $a = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0, 7, 9, 1\\}$, here are all their prefixes and their dynamic programming array. Notice, that the values of the array don't always change at the end.
$$ \begin{array}{ll} \text{prefix} = \\{\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, \infty, \dots\\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 8, \infty, \dots\\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 3, \infty, \dots\\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 3, 4, \infty, \dots\\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 3, 4, 6, \infty, \dots\\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 3, 4, 5, \infty, \dots\\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 2, 4, 5, \infty, \dots \\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 0, 4, 5, \infty, \dots \\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0, 7\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 0, 4, 5, 7, \infty, \dots \\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0, 7, 9\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 0, 4, 5, 7, 9, \infty, \dots \\}\\\ \text{prefix} = \\{8, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0, 7, 9, 1\\} &\quad d = \\{-\infty, 0, 1, 5, 7, 9, \infty, \dots \\}\\\ \end{array} $$
When we process $a[i]$, we can ask ourselves. What have the conditions to be, that we write the current number $a[i]$ into the $d[0 \dots n]$ array?
We set $d[l] = a[i]$, if there is a longest increasing sequence of length $l$ that ends in $a[i]$, and there is no longest increasing sequence of length $l$ that ends in a smaller number. Similar to the previous approach, if we remove the number $a[i]$ from the longest increasing sequence of length $l$, we get another longest increasing sequence of length $l -1$. So we want to extend a longest increasing sequence of length $l - 1$ by the number $a[i]$, and obviously the longest increasing sequence of length $l - 1$ that ends with the smallest element will work the best, in other words the sequence of length $l-1$ that ends in element $d[l-1]$.
There is a longest increasing sequence of length $l - 1$ that we can extend with the number $a[i]$, exactly if $d[l-1] < a[i]$. So we can just iterate over each length $l$, and check if we can extend a longest increasing sequence of length $l - 1$ by checking the criteria.
Additionally we also need to check, if we maybe have already found a longest increasing sequence of length $l$ with a smaller number at the end. So we only update if $a[i] < d[l]$.
After processing all the elements of $a[]$ the length of the desired subsequence is the largest $l$ with $d[l] < \infty$.
```
int lis(vector<int> const& a) {
    int n = a.size();
    const int INF = 1e9;
    vector<int> d(n+1, INF);
    d[0] = -INF;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int l = 1; l <= n; l++) {
            if (d[l-1] < a[i] && a[i] < d[l])
                d[l] = a[i];
        }
    }

    int ans = 0;
    for (int l = 0; l <= n; l++) {
        if (d[l] < INF)
            ans = l;
    }
    return ans;
}

```

We now make two important observations.
  1. The array $d$ will always be sorted: $d[l-1] < d[l]$ for all $i = 1 \dots n$.
This is trivial, as you can just remove the last element from the increasing subsequence of length $l$, and you get a increasing subsequence of length $l-1$ with a smaller ending number.
  2. The element $a[i]$ will only update at most one value $d[l]$.
This follows immediately from the above implementation. There can only be one place in the array with $d[l-1] < a[i] < d[l]$.


Thus we can find this element in the array $d[]$ using [binary search](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) in $O(\log n)$. In fact we can simply look in the array $d[]$ for the first number that is strictly greater than $a[i]$, and we try to update this element in the same way as the above implementation.
### Implementation[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#implementation_1 "Permanent link")
This gives us the improved $O(n \log n)$ implementation:
```
int lis(vector<int> const& a) {
    int n = a.size();
    const int INF = 1e9;
    vector<int> d(n+1, INF);
    d[0] = -INF;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int l = upper_bound(d.begin(), d.end(), a[i]) - d.begin();
        if (d[l-1] < a[i] && a[i] < d[l])
            d[l] = a[i];
    }

    int ans = 0;
    for (int l = 0; l <= n; l++) {
        if (d[l] < INF)
            ans = l;
    }
    return ans;
}

```

### Restoring the subsequence[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#restoring-the-subsequence_1 "Permanent link")
It is also possible to restore the subsequence using this approach. This time we have to maintain two auxiliary arrays. One that tells us the index of the elements in $d[]$. And again we have to create an array of "ancestors" $p[i]$. $p[i]$ will be the index of the previous element for the optimal subsequence ending in element $i$.
It's easy to maintain these two arrays in the course of iteration over the array $a[]$ alongside the computations of $d[]$. And at the end it is not difficult to restore the desired subsequence using these arrays.
## Solution in $O(n \log n)$ with data structures[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#solution-in-on-log-n-with-data-structures "Permanent link")
Instead of the above method for computing the longest increasing subsequence in $O(n \log n)$ we can also solve the problem in a different way: using some simple data structures.
Let's go back to the first method. Remember that $d[i]$ is the value $d[j] + 1$ with $j < i$ and $a[j] < a[i]$.
Thus if we define an additional array $t[]$ such that
$$t[a[i]] = d[i],$$
then the problem of computing the value $d[i]$ is equivalent to finding the **maximum value in a prefix** of the array $t[]$:
$$d[i] = \max\left(t[0 \dots a[i] - 1] + 1\right)$$
The problem of finding the maximum of a prefix of an array (which changes) is a standard problem that can be solved by many different data structures. For instance we can use a [Segment tree](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/segment_tree.html) or a [Fenwick tree](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/fenwick.html).
This method has obviously some **shortcomings** : in terms of length and complexity of the implementation this approach will be worse than the method using binary search. In addition if the input numbers $a[i]$ are especially large, then we would have to use some tricks, like compressing the numbers (i.e. renumber them from $0$ to $n-1$), or use a dynamic segment tree (only generate the branches of the tree that are important). Otherwise the memory consumption will be too high.
On the other hand this method has also some **advantages** : with this method you don't have to think about any tricky properties in the dynamic programming solution. And this approach allows us to generalize the problem very easily (see below).
## Related tasks[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#related-tasks "Permanent link")
Here are several problems that are closely related to the problem of finding the longest increasing subsequence.
### Longest non-decreasing subsequence[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#longest-non-decreasing-subsequence "Permanent link")
This is in fact nearly the same problem. Only now it is allowed to use identical numbers in the subsequence.
The solution is essentially also nearly the same. We just have to change the inequality signs, and make a slight modification to the binary search.
### Number of longest increasing subsequences[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#number-of-longest-increasing-subsequences "Permanent link")
We can use the first discussed method, either the $O(n^2)$ version or the version using data structures. We only have to additionally store in how many ways we can obtain longest increasing subsequences ending in the values $d[i]$.
The number of ways to form a longest increasing subsequences ending in $a[i]$ is the sum of all ways for all longest increasing subsequences ending in $j$ where $d[j]$ is maximal. There can be multiple such $j$, so we need to sum all of them.
Using a Segment tree this approach can also be implemented in $O(n \log n)$.
It is not possible to use the binary search approach for this task.
### Smallest number of non-increasing subsequences covering a sequence[¶](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html#smallest-number-of-non-increasing-subsequences-covering-a-sequence "Permanent link")
For a given array with $n$ numbers $a[0 \dots n - 1]$ we have to colorize the numbers in the smallest number of colors, so that each color forms a non-increasing subsequence.
To solve this, we notice that the minimum number of required colors is equal to the length of the longest increasing subsequence.
**Proof** : We need to prove the **duality** of these two problems.
Let's denote by $x$ the length of the longest increasing subsequence and by $y$ the least number of non-increasing subsequences that form a cover. We need to prove that $x = y$.
It is clear that $y < x$ is not possible, because if we have $x$ strictly increasing elements, than no two can be part of the same non-increasing subsequence. Therefore we have $y \ge x$.
We now show that $y > x$ is not possible by contradiction. Suppose that $y > x$. Then we consider any optimal set of $y$ non-increasing subsequences. We transform this in set in the following way: as long as there are two such subsequences such that the first begins before the second subsequence, and the first sequence start with a number greater than or equal to the second, then we unhook this starting number and attach it to the beginning of second. After a finite number of steps we have $y$ subsequences, and their starting numbers will form an increasing subsequence of length $y$. Since we assumed that $y > x$ we reached a contradiction.
Thus it follows that $y = x$.
**Restoring the sequences** : The desired partition of the sequence into subsequences can be done greedily. I.e. go from left to right and assign the current number or that subsequence ending with the minimal number which is greater than or equal to the current one.

# 背包 DP
前置知识：[动态规划部分简介](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/)。
## 引入[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E5%BC%95%E5%85%A5 "Permanent link")
在具体讲何为「背包 dp」前，先来看如下的例题：
[「USACO07 DEC」Charm Bracelet](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P2871)
题意概要：有 𝑛n![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品和一个容量为 𝑊W![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的背包，每个物品有重量 𝑤𝑖wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 和价值 𝑣𝑖vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 两种属性，要求选若干物品放入背包使背包中物品的总价值最大且背包中物品的总重量不超过背包的容量。
在上述例题中，由于每个物体只有两种可能的状态（取与不取），对应二进制中的 00![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 和 11![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，这类问题便被称为「0-1 背包问题」。
## 0-1 背包[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#0-1-%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85 "Permanent link")
### 解释[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E8%A7%A3%E9%87%8A "Permanent link")
例题中已知条件有第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品的重量 𝑤𝑖wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，价值 𝑣𝑖vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，以及背包的总容量 𝑊W![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。
设 DP 状态 𝑓𝑖,𝑗fi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 为在只能放前 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品的情况下，容量为 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的背包所能达到的最大总价值。
考虑转移。假设当前已经处理好了前 𝑖−1i−1![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品的所有状态，那么对于第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品，当其不放入背包时，背包的剩余容量不变，背包中物品的总价值也不变，故这种情况的最大价值为 𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗fi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)；当其放入背包时，背包的剩余容量会减小 𝑤𝑖wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，背包中物品的总价值会增大 𝑣𝑖vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，故这种情况的最大价值为 𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑤𝑖+𝑣𝑖fi−1,j−wi+vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。
由此可以得出状态转移方程：
𝑓𝑖,𝑗=max(𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗,𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑤𝑖+𝑣𝑖)fi,j=max(fi−1,j,fi−1,j−wi+vi)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
这里如果直接采用二维数组对状态进行记录，会出现 MLE。可以考虑改用滚动数组的形式来优化。
由于对 𝑓𝑖fi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 有影响的只有 𝑓𝑖−1fi−1![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，可以去掉第一维，直接用 𝑓𝑖fi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 来表示处理到当前物品时背包容量为 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的最大价值，得出以下方程：
𝑓𝑗=max(𝑓𝑗,𝑓𝑗−𝑤𝑖+𝑣𝑖)fj=max(fj,fj−wi+vi)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
**务必牢记并理解这个转移方程，因为大部分背包问题的转移方程都是在此基础上推导出来的。**

## 完全背包[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E5%AE%8C%E5%85%A8%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85 "Permanent link")
### 解释[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E8%A7%A3%E9%87%8A_1 "Permanent link")
完全背包模型与 0-1 背包类似，与 0-1 背包的区别仅在于一个物品可以选取无限次，而非仅能选取一次。
我们可以借鉴 0-1 背包的思路，进行状态定义：设 𝑓𝑖,𝑗fi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 为只能选前 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品时，容量为 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的背包可以达到的最大价值。
需要注意的是，虽然定义与 0-1 背包类似，但是其状态转移方程与 0-1 背包并不相同。
### 过程[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E8%BF%87%E7%A8%8B "Permanent link")
可以考虑一个朴素的做法：对于第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 件物品，枚举其选了多少个来转移。这样做的时间复杂度是 𝑂(𝑛3)O(n3)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的。
状态转移方程如下：
𝑓𝑖,𝑗=+∞max𝑘=0(𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑘×𝑤𝑖+𝑣𝑖×𝑘)fi,j=maxk=0+∞(fi−1,j−k×wi+vi×k)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
考虑做一个简单的优化。可以发现，对于 𝑓𝑖,𝑗fi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，只要通过 𝑓𝑖,𝑗−𝑤𝑖fi,j−wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 转移就可以了。因此状态转移方程为：
𝑓𝑖,𝑗=max(𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗,𝑓𝑖,𝑗−𝑤𝑖+𝑣𝑖)fi,j=max(fi−1,j,fi,j−wi+vi)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
理由是当我们这样转移时，𝑓𝑖,𝑗−𝑤𝑖fi,j−wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 已经由 𝑓𝑖,𝑗−2×𝑤𝑖fi,j−2×wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 更新过，那么 𝑓𝑖,𝑗−𝑤𝑖fi,j−wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 就是充分考虑了第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 件物品所选次数后得到的最优结果。换言之，我们通过局部最优子结构的性质重复使用了之前的枚举过程，优化了枚举的复杂度。
与 0-1 背包相同，我们可以将第一维去掉来优化空间复杂度。如果理解了 0-1 背包的优化方式，就不难明白压缩后的循环是正向的（也就是上文中提到的错误优化）。
[「Luogu P1616」疯狂的采药](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P1616)

## 多重背包[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E5%A4%9A%E9%87%8D%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85 "Permanent link")
多重背包也是 0-1 背包的一个变式。与 0-1 背包的区别在于每种物品有 𝑘𝑖ki![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个，而非一个。
一个很朴素的想法就是：把「每种物品选 𝑘𝑖ki![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 次」等价转换为「有 𝑘𝑖ki![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个相同的物品，每个物品选一次」。这样就转换成了一个 0-1 背包模型，套用上文所述的方法就可已解决。状态转移方程如下：
𝑓𝑖,𝑗=𝑘𝑖max𝑘=0(𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑘×𝑤𝑖+𝑣𝑖×𝑘)fi,j=maxk=0ki(fi−1,j−k×wi+vi×k)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
时间复杂度 𝑂(𝑊∑𝑛𝑖=1𝑘𝑖)O(W∑i=1nki)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。
核心代码
```

2

for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
  for (int weight = W; weight >= w[i]; weight--) {
    // 多遍历一层物品数量
    for (int k = 1; k * w[i] <= weight && k <= cnt[i]; k++) {
      dp[weight] = max(dp[weight], dp[weight - k * w[i]] + k * v[i]);
    }
  }
}

### 二进制分组优化[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E4%BA%8C%E8%BF%9B%E5%88%B6%E5%88%86%E7%BB%84%E4%BC%98%E5%8C%96 "Permanent link")
考虑优化。我们仍考虑把多重背包转化成 0-1 背包模型来求解。
### 解释[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E8%A7%A3%E9%87%8A_2 "Permanent link")
显然，复杂度中的 𝑂(𝑛𝑊)O(nW)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 部分无法再优化了，我们只能从 𝑂(∑𝑘𝑖)O(∑ki)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 处入手。为了表述方便，我们用 𝐴𝑖,𝑗Ai,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 代表第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 种物品拆分出的第 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品。
在朴素的做法中，∀𝑗≤𝑘𝑖∀j≤ki![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，𝐴𝑖,𝑗Ai,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 均表示相同物品。那么我们效率低的原因主要在于我们进行了大量重复性的工作。举例来说，我们考虑了「同时选 𝐴𝑖,1,𝐴𝑖,2Ai,1,Ai,2![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)」与「同时选 𝐴𝑖,2,𝐴𝑖,3Ai,2,Ai,3![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)」这两个完全等效的情况。这样的重复性工作我们进行了许多次。那么优化拆分方式就成为了解决问题的突破口。
### 过程[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E8%BF%87%E7%A8%8B_1 "Permanent link")
我们可以通过「二进制分组」的方式使拆分方式更加优美。
具体地说就是令 𝐴𝑖,𝑗(𝑗∈[0,⌊log2⁡(𝑘𝑖+1)⌋−1])Ai,j(j∈[0,⌊log2⁡(ki+1)⌋−1])![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 分别表示由 2𝑗2j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个单个物品「捆绑」而成的大物品。特殊地，若 𝑘𝑖+1ki+1![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 不是 22![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的整数次幂，则需要在最后添加一个由 𝑘𝑖−2⌊log2⁡(𝑘𝑖+1)⌋−1ki−2⌊log2⁡(ki+1)⌋−1![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个单个物品「捆绑」而成的大物品用于补足。
举几个例子：
  * 6=1+2+36=1+2+3![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
  * 8=1+2+4+18=1+2+4+1![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
  * 18=1+2+4+8+318=1+2+4+8+3![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
  * 31=1+2+4+8+1631=1+2+4+8+16![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)


显然，通过上述拆分方式，可以表示任意 ≤𝑘𝑖≤ki![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品的等效选择方式。将每种物品按照上述方式拆分后，使用 0-1 背包的方法解决即可。
时间复杂度 𝑂(𝑊∑𝑛𝑖=1log2⁡𝑘𝑖)O(W∑i=1nlog2⁡ki)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)

有 𝑛n![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个任务需要完成，完成第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个任务需要花费 𝑡𝑖ti![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 分钟，产生 𝑐𝑖ci![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 元的开支。
现在有 𝑇T![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 分钟时间，𝑊W![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 元钱来处理这些任务，求最多能完成多少任务。
这道题是很明显的 0-1 背包问题，可是不同的是选一个物品会消耗两种价值（经费、时间），只需在状态中增加一维存放第二种价值即可。
这时候就要注意，再开一维存放物品编号就不合适了，因为容易 MLE。

for (int k = 1; k <= n; k++)
  for (int i = m; i >= mi; i--)    // 对经费进行一层枚举
    for (int j = t; j >= ti; j--)  // 对时间进行一层枚举
      dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j], dp[i - mi][j - ti] + 1);

```

## 分组背包[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E5%88%86%E7%BB%84%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85 "Permanent link")
[「Luogu P1757」通天之分组背包](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P1757)
有 𝑛n![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 件物品和一个大小为 𝑚m![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的背包，第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品的价值为 𝑤𝑖wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，体积为 𝑣𝑖vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。同时，每个物品属于一个组，同组内最多只能选择一个物品。求背包能装载物品的最大总价值。
这种题怎么想呢？其实是从「在所有物品中选择一件」变成了「从当前组中选择一件」，于是就对每一组进行一次 0-1 背包就可以了。
再说一说如何进行存储。我们可以将 𝑡𝑘,𝑖tk,i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 表示第 𝑘k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 组的第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 件物品的编号是多少，再用 cnt𝑘cntk![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 表示第 𝑘k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 组物品有多少个。
### 实现[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E5%AE%9E%E7%8E%B0_3 "Permanent link")
[C++](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#__tabbed_5_1)[Python](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#__tabbed_5_2)
```
1

```
| ```
for (int k = 1; k <= ts; k++)          // 循环每一组
  for (int i = m; i >= 0; i--)         // 循环背包容量
    for (int j = 1; j <= cnt[k]; j++)  // 循环该组的每一个物品
      if (i >= w[t[k][j]])             // 背包容量充足
        dp[i] = max(dp[i],
                    dp[i - w[t[k][j]]] + c[t[k][j]]);  // 像0-1背包一样状态转移

```

    for i in range(m, -1, -1):  # 循环背包容量
        for j in range(1, cnt[k] + 1):  # 循环该组的每一个物品

                    dp[i], dp[i - w[t[k][j]]] + c[t[k][j]]

## 有依赖的背包[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E6%9C%89%E4%BE%9D%E8%B5%96%E7%9A%84%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85 "Permanent link")
[「Luogu P1064」金明的预算方案](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P1064)
金明有 𝑛n![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 元钱，想要买 𝑚m![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品，第 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 件物品的价格为 𝑣𝑖vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，重要度为 𝑝𝑖pi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。有些物品是从属于某个主件物品的附件，要买这个物品，必须购买它的主件。
目标是让所有购买的物品的 𝑣𝑖×𝑝𝑖vi×pi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 之和最大。
考虑分类讨论。对于一个主件和它的若干附件，有以下几种可能：只买主件，买主件 + 某些附件。因为这几种可能性只能选一种，所以可以将这看成分组背包。
如果是多叉树的集合，则要先算子节点的集合，最后算父节点的集合。
## 泛化物品的背包[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E6%B3%9B%E5%8C%96%E7%89%A9%E5%93%81%E7%9A%84%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85 "Permanent link")
这种背包，没有固定的费用和价值，它的价值是随着分配给它的费用而定。在背包容量为 𝑉V![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的背包问题中，当分配给它的费用为 𝑣𝑖vi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 时，能得到的价值就是 ℎ(𝑣𝑖)h(vi)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。这时，将固定的价值换成函数的引用即可。
## 杂项[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E6%9D%82%E9%A1%B9 "Permanent link")
### 小优化[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E5%B0%8F%E4%BC%98%E5%8C%96 "Permanent link")
根据贪心原理，当费用相同时，只需保留价值最高的；当价值一定时，只需保留费用最低的；当有两件物品 𝑖,𝑗i,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 且 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的价值大于 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的价值并且 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的费用小于 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的费用时，只需保留 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。

#### 求方案数[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E6%B1%82%E6%96%B9%E6%A1%88%E6%95%B0 "Permanent link")
对于给定的一个背包容量、物品费用、其他关系等的问题，求装到一定容量的方案总数。
这种问题就是把求最大值换成求和即可。
例如 0-1 背包问题的转移方程就变成了：
dp𝑖=∑(dp𝑖,dp𝑖−𝑐𝑖)dpi=∑(dpi,dpi−ci)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
初始条件：dp0=1dp0=1![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)
因为当容量为 00![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 时也有一个方案，即什么都不装。
#### 求最优方案总数[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E6%B1%82%E6%9C%80%E4%BC%98%E6%96%B9%E6%A1%88%E6%80%BB%E6%95%B0 "Permanent link")
要求最优方案总数，我们要对 0-1 背包里的 dpdp![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 数组的定义稍作修改，DP 状态 𝑓𝑖,𝑗fi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 为在只能放前 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品的情况下，容量为 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的背包「正好装满」所能达到的最大总价值。
这样修改之后，每一种 DP 状态都可以用一个 𝑔𝑖,𝑗gi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 来表示方案数。
𝑓𝑖,𝑗fi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 表示只考虑前 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品时背包体积「正好」是 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 时的最大价值。
𝑔𝑖,𝑗gi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 表示只考虑前 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品时背包体积「正好」是 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 时的方案数。
转移方程：
如果 𝑓𝑖,𝑗=𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗fi,j=fi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 且 𝑓𝑖,𝑗≠𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑣+𝑤fi,j≠fi−1,j−v+w![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 说明我们此时不选择把物品放入背包更优，方案数由 𝑔𝑖−1,𝑗gi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 转移过来，
如果 𝑓𝑖,𝑗≠𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗fi,j≠fi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 且 𝑓𝑖,𝑗=𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑣+𝑤fi,j=fi−1,j−v+w![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 说明我们此时选择把物品放入背包更优，方案数由 𝑔𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑣gi−1,j−v![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 转移过来，
如果 𝑓𝑖,𝑗=𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗fi,j=fi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 且 𝑓𝑖,𝑗=𝑓𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑣+𝑤fi,j=fi−1,j−v+w![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 说明放入或不放入都能取得最优解，方案数由 𝑔𝑖−1,𝑗gi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 和 𝑔𝑖−1,𝑗−𝑣gi−1,j−v![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 转移过来。

for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
  for (int j = V; j >= v[i]; j--) {
    int tmp = std::max(dp[j], dp[j - v[i]] + w[i]);
    int c = 0;
    if (tmp == dp[j]) c += cnt[j];                       // 如果从dp[j]转移
    if (tmp == dp[j - v[i]] + w[i]) c += cnt[j - v[i]];  // 如果从dp[j-v[i]]转移
    dp[j] = tmp;
    cnt[j] = c;
  }
}
int max = 0;  // 寻找最优解
for (int i = 0; i <= V; i++) {
  max = std::max(max, dp[i]);
}
int res = 0;
for (int i = 0; i <= V; i++) {
  if (dp[i] == max) {
    res += cnt[i];  // 求和最优解方案数
  }
}

#### 背包的第 k 优解[](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/#%E8%83%8C%E5%8C%85%E7%9A%84%E7%AC%AC-k-%E4%BC%98%E8%A7%A3 "Permanent link")
普通的 0-1 背包是要求最优解，在普通的背包 DP 方法上稍作改动，增加一维用于记录当前状态下的前 k 优解，即可得到求 0-1 背包第 𝑘k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 优解的算法。 具体来讲：dpi,j,kdpi,j,k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 记录了前 𝑖i![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 个物品中，选择的物品总体积为 𝑗j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 时，能够得到的第 𝑘k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 大的价值和。这个状态可以理解为将普通 0-1 背包只用记录一个数据的 dpi,jdpi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 扩展为记录一个有序的优解序列。转移时，普通背包最优解的求法是 dpi,j=max(dpi−1,j,dpi−1,j−vi+𝑤𝑖)dpi,j=max(dpi−1,j,dpi−1,j−vi+wi)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，现在我们则是要合并 dpi−1,jdpi−1,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)，dpi−1,j−vi+𝑤𝑖dpi−1,j−vi+wi![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 这两个大小为 𝑘k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的递减序列，并保留合并后前 𝑘k![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 大的价值记在 dpi,jdpi,j![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 里，这一步利用双指针法，复杂度是 𝑂(𝑘)O(k)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的，整体时间复杂度为 𝑂(𝑛𝑚𝑘)O(nmk)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/)。空间上，此方法与普通背包一样可以压缩掉第一维，复杂度是 𝑂(𝑚𝑘)O(mk)![](https://oi-wiki.org/dp/knapsack/) 的。

memset(dp, 0, sizeof(dp));
int i, j, p, x, y, z;
scanf("%d%d%d", &n, &m, &K);
for (i = 0; i < n; i++) scanf("%d", &w[i]);
for (i = 0; i < n; i++) scanf("%d", &c[i]);
for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  for (j = m; j >= c[i]; j--) {
    for (p = 1; p <= K; p++) {
      a[p] = dp[j - c[i]][p] + w[i];
      b[p] = dp[j][p];
    }
    a[p] = b[p] = -1;
    x = y = z = 1;
    while (z <= K && (a[x] != -1 || b[y] != -1)) {
      if (a[x] > b[y])
        dp[j][z] = a[x++];
      else
        dp[j][z] = b[y++];
      if (dp[j][z] != dp[j][z - 1]) z++;
    }
  }
}
printf("%d\n", dp[m][K]);
